comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C91-C93 regarding HNF4A/SOX9 regulon analysis in human data. Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes it's computational inference without functional validation; peer reviewers accept it as supporting clinical relevance.

Strong agreement on claims C9-C10, C88-C90 regarding inverse relationship between HNF4A and LYZ+ cells in vivo. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=3); peer reviewers accept the data but question functional significance in broader context.

Agreement on claims C6, C69-C70, C72-C76 regarding HNF4A identification through bioinformatics. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes convergent multi-omics evidence; peer reviewers accept the pathway analysis without challenge.

Divergent evaluations on claims C7, C83-C87 regarding HNF4A-Sox9 mechanistic link. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED based on ChIP-seq and rescue experiments; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting additional in vivo loss-of-function and overexpression experiments to validate Sox9 as central regulator.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C35, C95, C118, C120 regarding metastasis reduction. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multiple readouts and statistical rigor; peer reviewers describe data as 'interesting and convincing' with solid evidence.

Significant divergence on claims C2, C11, C36, C117, C125 regarding overall integrative conclusions. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED with convergent evidence; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting more direct functional experiments to test Paneth-like cell role and questioning whether splenic injection model appropriately addresses the pathway.

Agreement on claims C4, C30, C41, C48, C51-C52 regarding LYZ+ cell reduction. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes temporal analysis and rescue experiments; peer reviewers accept the data but Reviewer 2 questions functional significance given low Paneth cell numbers (17 cells) in scRNA-seq.

Divergent evaluations on claims C5, C32, C54-C56, C60 regarding scRNA-seq identification of LYZ+ cells. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED based on clustering and pathway analysis; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 expressing concern that 17 Paneth cells is insufficient to drive the observed differences.

Agreement on claim C122 regarding therapeutic implications. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as speculative without validation; peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED but acknowledge it's prospective rather than experimentally validated. Both recognize this as future-oriented rather than demonstrated.

Divergent evaluations on claims C62-C65, C68 regarding human scRNA-seq analysis. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED based on reanalysis of published data; peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to concerns about low Paneth cell numbers (17 cells) questioning whether this population can drive the observed differences.

Agreement on claims C37-C39 regarding confirmatory DKK2 findings. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes these in broader metastasis analysis; peer reviewers accept as established background consistent with prior work.

Agreement on claims C45-C47 regarding RNA-seq showing niche disruption. Both find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes temporal analysis; peer reviewers accept as supporting evidence for stem cell niche formation narrative.

Partial overlap on claims C115, C124 regarding mechanistic summary. OpenEval finds summary statements SUPPORTED by experimental data; peer reviewers rate the broader mechanism UNCERTAIN, requesting double knockout experiments for more direct evidence of HNF4A protein stabilization as crucial mechanism.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C1, C12-C29 as SUPPORTED by appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not assess background/context claims.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims C42-C44, C57-C59, C61, C67, C77-C82, C96-C116 as SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are contextual rather than novel findings.

OpenEval evaluates claims C8, C49-C50, C71, C123 citing prior work as SUPPORTED. No direct peer review evaluation, though peer reviewers reference this prior work (Shin et al., 2021a) when discussing mechanistic context.
